text:
Hello,

When I signed my lease with Kirschbaum Holdings Ltd for the flat at Hauptstrasse 107 in Burgdorf in December 2021, the agent explained that the rent would go up in fixed steps. It is written in the contract: CHF 80 more per month every two years, on 1 April, starting from CHF 1240. I accepted that at the time because the starting rent was low. What is happening now is supposed to be the second of those steps.

There is nothing else in the lease about how the rent can change. It isn't tied to inflation or the consumer price index or anything of that kind, only to those fixed steps.

I have attached the envelope and the post office receipt that show when the letter reached me.

The letter is from Mr David Widmer and I signed for it on 27 January 2026. He writes that from 1 April 2026 my rent will be CHF 1400 a month instead of CHF 1320. So on paper it is exactly the step in the contract. My question is whether they can really just keep doing this. Money is tight for me since I went down to 60 percent at work, and CHF 80 more each month adds up quickly. A friend of mine, Grace Frei, thought these step increases are only allowed under certain conditions and that I should get advice before simply paying.

I have also attached the lease so you can read the clause yourself.

Thank you in advance,
Rachel Egli
